From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin *imparāre, from in- +‎ parāre. Compare French emparer (“to seize”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /im.paˈra.re/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -are
  • Hyphenation: im‧pa‧rà‧re

Verb

[edit]

imparàre (first-person singular present impàro, first-person singular past historic imparài, past participle imparàto, auxiliary avére) (transitive)

  1. to learn
    imparare l'inglese ― to learn English
    imparare a leggere e scrivere ― to learn to read and write
  2. (Romanesco) to teach
